patch.value: Disable cmd.exe delayed expansion on the Windows pm launch path

pmLaunchPlan builds ["/d", "/s", "/c", tail] with no /v:off. assertNoCmdVariableExpansion refuses literal ", \r/\n, and %NAME% pairs but does not refuse or neutralise !NAME!. Delayed expansion is off by default but can be switched on machine-wide via HKLM\Software\Microsoft\Command Processor\DelayedExpansion or inherited from a parent cmd /v:on. When on, !NAME! expands inside the quote state exactly like %NAME%, so --pm-path "C:\work\!BUILD!\pm" silently becomes a different path, pm reads a different workspace, and the standup is built from it while reporting success — the precise failure the %NAME% refusal already exists to prevent. The fix inserts /v:off before /c so ! is literal regardless of the machine registry setting, preferred over a !NAME! refusal because ! is a legal Windows filename character.

Inserted /v:off before /c in pmLaunchPlan's win32 argv so delayed expansion is disabled for the launch regardless of the machine's DelayedExpansion registry setting or a parent cmd /v:on. Updated doc comments on pmLaunchPlan, assertNoCmdVariableExpansion, and quoteWindowsArg to state the complete boundary: the launch disables delayed expansion so ! is literal, and no argument may contain a literal quote, line break, or %NAME% pair. Preferred /v:off over a !NAME! refusal because ! is a legal Windows filename character. Updated existing win32 launch tests for the new /v:off argv element; added two regression tests asserting /v:off appears before /c and that !NAME! still launches verbatim. Source-only revert (git stash of index.ts) produced exactly the two new tests failing: '/v:off must be present in the launch argv' and 'the !NAME! pair must survive verbatim into the tail'. Build, test, typecheck, coverage, docstring, and changelog:check gates passed.
